adjudications.evidence_summary: process_payment executes and commits an unconditional INSERT for every invocation, while the charges schema has no uniqueness constraint on request_id. The targeted idempotency test calls the function twice with request_id req-123 and observes two rows rather than one.
adjudications.scope_assessment: The failure occurs in the supplied implementation under the retry behavior explicitly exercised by the case test, so it applies to supported usage rather than a hypothetical caller or infrastructure assumption.
adjudications.materiality_assessment: A retry duplicates a payment charge, creating a concrete financial side effect and a production data-integrity and correctness risk; high severity is warranted.

findings.claim: Retrying the same payment request creates a second charge instead of returning the original charge outcome, allowing retries to duplicate a financial side effect.
evidence: evals/cases/case_02/src/payments.py:14-18 unconditionally inserts and commits a new charges row on every process_payment call without checking for an existing request_id.
evals/cases/case_02/src/db.py:9-13 declares request_id NOT NULL but does not enforce uniqueness, permitting multiple charges for the same logical request.
pytest -q evals/cases/case_02 fails test_idempotency.py:18 because two calls with request_id req-123 produce count == 2 instead of the required count == 1; the single-request test passes.
